minutes.headline: Board appointed Faith Beal to the PAC and John Reynolds to the Sewer Commission, and voted to send a Chapter 61 letter.
minutes.summary: With the town manager on vacation, the board made two appointments: Faith Beal to the PAC (cable committee) and, in a joint meeting, John Reynolds to the Sewer Commission. It voted to send a letter saying the Chapter 61 removal notice was not in compliance. It also heard a transit schedule and fare update and a round of committee reports.

budget_items.what_was_said: One warrant for accounts payable was read.
Changing from five loops to seven is cost-neutral to the town for the fiscal year, and fares were raised for the first time in years.
The regional planning agency received a brownfields grant that might be usable for cleaning up a gas station property.
A company donated money to the middle school for computer purchases.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to send a letter stating the Chapter 61 removal notification was not in compliance.
In a joint meeting, the board voted unanimously to appoint a member to the Sewer Commission.
The board voted to appoint a member to the PAC, the town's cable committee.
The board heard that moving the transit route from five loops to seven is cost-neutral to the town for the fiscal year, and that fares were raised.
The board will discuss next week appointing a screening committee for the building reuse RFQ.

why_it_matters: The Chapter 61 letter bears on how the town handles notice about land leaving a preferential tax classification, which can affect whether the town gets a chance to act on the land.
The transit change affects riders' fares and service frequency, with no added cost to the town budget, mostly taxes, for the fiscal year.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board discussion of a screening committee for the building reuse RFQ.
A possible meeting with town counsel on the level of service, and a possible joint meeting with the Townsend selectmen on the pipeline response.
